source.title: Promote, Suppress, Iterate: How Language Models Answer One-to-Many Factual Queries

page_placements.theme: MLP layers also suppress already-promoted or earlier tokens, depending on upstream attention

record.tranche_reason: Extends analysis of suppression to one-to-many factual queries in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, using component and token-level analyses rather than testing the GPT-2 small L10H7 circuit.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative results on attention and MLP suppression of previous answers, and on attention-head promotion and suppression rates. Its cited findings about GPT-2 small L10H7 are background only and are not recorded as results. Causal-tracing probability changes establish token importance, but do not directly measure suppression, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: In Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, the study measures attention outputs on tokens that earlier MLPs promote and that already appear in the context. It finds that late-layer attention gives these previous answers negative logits. That is copy-suppression behaviour in other models and a new task, so it bears on V5. It does not examine GPT-2 small L10H7, calibration or self-repair.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the models promote all answers and then suppress previously generated ones. Late-layer attention attends to and suppresses prior answers, MLPs amplify that suppression, and MLPs also use previous answers to promote new ones.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses early decoding, Token Lens, causal tracing, and attention knockout to analyze one-to-many factual recall in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2. It does not reproduce the GPT-2 small L10H7 circuit analysis or measure that head's contribution to loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Answer promotion by attention is more evident for Country-Cities than for Artist-Songs and Actor-Movies. The paper reports analysis across three prompt templates, but notes that further work is needed to establish generalization across templates.

fits_no_version.finding: MLPs amplify suppression of previous answers. After attention to those answers is knocked out, MLP logits for previous answers rise, while MLP logits for new answers fall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Copy-suppression signals from attention are amplified by downstream MLPs, which also use previous answers to promote new ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-head promotion and suppression rates correlate positively, and most heads fall in the low-rate region.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these models, promotion and suppression are distributed across many heads rather than held by dedicated suppression heads.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The analyses focus only on correct model responses. The authors note that early decoding with the final unembedding may be less reliable, particularly in early layers, and that broader prompt-template generalization needs further study. The reported suppression findings are mainly qualitative rather than accompanied by uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported suppression results were left out. Other token-level analyses, such as subject-token effects and last-token promotion, do not directly measure previous-answer suppression.

untested.parts: GPT-2 small L10H7 is not studied.
There is no QK/OV circuit analysis and no measure of the share of loss explained.
Calibration and overconfidence are not measured.
No upstream copier is ablated and self-repair is not measured. The last-token knockout compensation (Fig. 6) involves MLPs and is not copy suppression.
Localizing individual negative heads, and showing that they share L10H7's QK/OV mechanism, is untested. IOI negative name movers are not examined.

missing.what: Attention suppression of previous answers holds at answer steps 4 and 5 (n=5, Actor-Movies, template 1). The appendix reports this separately for each model.
Per-model and per-dataset early-decoding results; Fig. 2 macro-averages across both models.

record.verdict_notes: The authors frame copy-suppression heads (McDougall et al.) as one candidate mechanism but never localize individual heads. All suppression evidence is qualitative, from logit-lens plots without uncertainty. The Limitations section says a single template was used per model and dataset, which contradicts the three templates in Tab. 2. Results cover correct cases only.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not study GPT-2 small L10H7 or test whether that head has one main role across the training distribution.
It does not analyze L10H7's QK or OV circuits or measure a share of loss explained.
It does not measure calibration or overconfidence from copying.
It does not ablate an upstream copier or measure self-repair.

It reports suppression of previous answers in other models and a different task, but does not localize individual negative heads or establish that they implement the same head-level circuit as GPT-2 small L10H7.
It does not measure self-repair or compare copy suppression's contribution with other self-repair mechanisms.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (macro-averaged)
rows.operation_detail: Early-decode attention outputs at the last token across layers.

conditions.value: macro-averaged across models, datasets, and templates

rows.measure: Logits for previously generated answer tokens
rows.baseline: Zero logit; negative logits indicate suppression
rows.value: Attention outputs negative logits for o(1) at step 2 and for o(1) and o(2) at step 3, starting from layer 28.
rows.note: Aggregate result across the two models; the paper also says attention suppresses previously generated answers in deeper layers.
rows.check: This is the summed output of the whole attention layer, not individual heads. The value is described qualitatively from Fig. 2, with no numbers given.

source_check.locator_found: §3.2; §4.1–§4.2, Fig. 2: negative attention logits beginning at layer 28 for previous answers at steps 2–3.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (macro-averaged)
rows.operation_detail: Early-decode MLP outputs at the last token across layers.

conditions.value: macro-averaged across models, datasets, and templates

rows.measure: Change in logits of previously generated answer tokens across layers
rows.value: MLPs decrease the logits of previous answers at the same deeper layers where attention suppresses them.
rows.note: The authors suggest this MLP suppression may leverage suppression signals from attention.
rows.check: This is MLP suppression, not an attention head. V5 concerns negative attention heads, so this row should not link to V5. It fits no version.

source_check.locator_found: §4.2, Fig. 2; Appendix C, Fig. 9: MLPs decrease previous-answer logits in deeper layers while generally promoting all answers.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (macro-averaged)
rows.operation_detail: Use Token Lens to decode attention outputs aggregated from previous answer tokens.

conditions.value: macro-averaged across models, datasets, and templates

rows.measure: Logits for the attended previous answer tokens
rows.baseline: Zero logit; negative logits indicate suppression
rows.value: Attention outputs negative logits for previous answer tokens in the final layers.
rows.note: The paper describes this as attention attending to and suppressing answers already present in the context.
rows.check: This is layer-level Token Lens summed over all heads, with no head localized. The locator should also cite §6.3 text and Fig. 20.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (macro-averaged)
rows.operation_detail: Knock out attention from the last token to previous answer tokens and compare MLP output logits before and after.

conditions.value: macro-averaged across models, datasets, and templates

rows.measure: MLP logit difference for previously generated answer tokens
rows.baseline: Zero difference; negative differences indicate suppression associated with the knocked-out tokens
rows.value: Previously generated answer tokens have negative MLP logit differences at late layers.
rows.note: The same analysis reports positive differences for new answers, indicating that prior answers also contribute to promoting new answers.
rows.check: This measures MLP logit differences after attention knockout, so it is MLP-level suppression, not head behaviour. It should not link to V5.

source_check.locator_found: §6.1 defines differences as original minus knockout logits; §6.3, Fig. 5; Appendix E, Fig. 21.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (macro-averaged)
rows.operation_detail: Classify attention heads by promotion and suppression rates using layer-wise logit thresholds.
rows.measure: Relationship between per-head promotion and suppression rates
rows.value: Promotion and suppression rates positively correlate; most plotted data points are concentrated in the bottom-left region.
rows.note: This aggregate head analysis does not identify an individual copy-suppression head.
rows.check: Head classification counts suppression of any token, including the subject, using a ±1σ threshold. It cannot show whether a dedicated copy-suppression head exists.

source_check.locator_found: §7.1–§7.2, Fig. 7: positively correlated rates, most points in the bottom-left region, template 1.

relationships.condition: Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2, one-to-many factual recall, late attention layers (around layer 28 onward), answer steps 2–3, macro-averaged over datasets and templates
relationships.reason: Previous answers, already promoted by MLPs and present in context, receive negative attention logits (R1). Attention to those tokens specifically suppresses them (R3). This is shown at whole-layer level, not per head.
relationships.display_finding: Previously promoted answers received negative attention logit contributions, and attention to those tokens suppressed them at the whole-layer level.

relation.reason: Early decoding and Token Lens provide original results on copy-suppression-like behavior in other models, bearing on V5.

tranche.reason: The paper measures suppression of already-promoted, in-context answers in a new task and two instruct-model families.

source_check.notes: The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate. §3.2 and figure captions specify three templates, although Limitations inconsistently says one; review status and cross-study counts or exclusivity cannot be verified from this text.

statements.correction: §7.1–§7.2, Fig. 7: promotion and suppression rates positively correlate; most points have low rates; classification uses any subject or answer token and layerwise mean ± one standard deviation; dedicated copy-suppression heads are neither identified nor ruled out.
statements.problem: The inference that suppression is distributed rather than performed by dedicated heads exceeds R5: its classification includes subject suppression and does not isolate suppression of previous answers.
